newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate down as "samba effect" eases.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate down as "samba effect" eases.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 150 basis points at 19.50 percent on Wednesday.
Analysts said investors returned to the market after a sell-off the day before once jitters faded over equity prices in Brazil.
"Rates opened very high due to what happened yesterday in Brazil, but demand for peso instruments surged at the close and rates thus fell," a fixed-income analyst said.
Dealers said demand for pesos could also be seen in a recovery by the peso.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts recouped 4.5 centavos from Tuesday's slide to end at 7.8750/7.8800 per dollar.
"Mexican currency seems to be in fashion and the market was hot today, investors really liked yesterday's increase in (secondary) rates," a trader said.

Overnight rates on bank paper declined in line with government rates and ended down 160 basis points at 19.90 percent. Banco de Mexico drained 889 million pesos from the market through three direct paper sales and two repos.
Liquidity of 1.490 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
